headline: S&P Revises Hungary's Rating Outlook to Stable on Lower Fiscal Risks
summary: S&P Global Ratings revised Hungary's credit outlook to stable from negative, citing improved fiscal frameworks and reforms under Prime Minister Peter Magyar that unlocked €16.4 billion in EU funds.
why: Sovereign credit outlook revisions reflect macroeconomic stabilization and lower fiscal deficit risks, lowering government borrowing costs.

impacts.name: Hungary
impacts.why: An improved sovereign credit outlook signals reduced financial risk and lower fiscal vulnerability.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: An upgrade in credit outlook reduces sovereign risk perception, bolstering investor confidence in Hungarian public finances and currency stability.
